summary: Masaaki Nohin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University, attested as an assistant professor between 1999 and 2003 and as a professor between 2013 and 2014.
Masaaki Tsuchiya specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University around 1979–1989 and held a post at Senshu University around 1996.

Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896), under Friedrich Max Müller (~1900), and at the University of Kiel under Paul Deussen (~1900–1902). He was a professor of religious studies at the University of Tokyo (1904) and lectured at the Collège de France (~1921).

Masaharu Imai specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Tokyo University of Education (~1961–1970), he held posts at Ibaraki University (~1981–1991) and the University of Tsukuba (~1991–2005).

Masahide Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University and earned his PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski at the University of London. He held posts at Nagoya University, Koyasan University, and Kanazawa University (~1996–2017).
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1974). He later served as an assistant professor at Ryukoku University (~1982–1992).

Masahiro Inami is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University (~1983–1988) and has held teaching positions at Tokyo Gakugei University since around 1993.

Masahiro Kusunoki (1921–2009) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1948–1953), he served as professor of religious studies and history of religion there (~1971–1985), and held leadership posts in related academic associations in the early 1980s.

Masahiro Shimoda is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his studies and doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1991–2023) and held visiting appointments at SOAS, Stanford, and the University of Virginia.
Masahiro Takano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and held a librarian post there, attested in 1995.

Masakazu Tanaka is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1980) and the London School of Economics and Political Science (~1980–1986, Ph.D.), and held a post at Kyoto University from 1988 to 2019.

Masako Keta is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1972–1982), she held posts at Aichi University of Technology Automotive Junior College, Kanazawa University (~1984–2000), and Kyoto University (~2000–2019) as professor of philosophy of religion.

Masamichi Ichigo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani, Kyoto, and Michigan, with teachers Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and as president of Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Vienna, where he studied under supervisor Helmut Krasser.

Masanori Nakagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held posts as a lecturer (attested 1991) and as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe (1915–2006) was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhism and religion. He studied at Osaka City and Kyoto Universities under Hajime Tanabe, Keiji Nishitani, Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, and D.T. Suzuki. He held posts at Nara University of Education, Kyoto, Nara, and PSR.
Masao Shizutani works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He held assistant professor posts at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

Masao Yamaguchi (1931–2013) was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He held positions at Chuo University, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1967–1992), University of Shizuoka, and Sapporo University.

Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as a professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002 and 2015).
